sub: Named after the jinn who listened to the Qur’an in ayah 1
theme: A group of jinn hear the Qur’an, believe, and reject shirk. The surah then calls people to worship Allah alone: the Prophet ﷺ only conveys, and only Allah knows the unseen.
story: Revealed in Makkah. When the Prophet ﷺ was sent, the jinn found the sky guarded. Flames drove them off whenever they tried to eavesdrop, so they spread out east and west to find the cause.

A group reached Nakhlah while the Prophet ﷺ was leading Fajr, reportedly on the way to the ʿUkāẓ market (other reports place it on his return from Ṭāʾif). They listened, believed and went back to warn their people. He never saw them; Allah told him.
Many Arabs then worshipped jinn and sought their protection. The surah corrects that, and makes clear the Prophet ﷺ only conveys the message and knows only the unseen Allah reveals to him.

sections.title: Jinn hear the Qur’an and believe; Allah has no wife or son
sections.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ is told that a group of jinn heard the Qur’an and believed. They declare that Allah has no wife or son, admit they once trusted the lies of their foolish ones, and recall how humans sought their protection, which only made things worse.
points: A group of jinn hears an amazing Qur’an and believes
Our Lord is exalted: no wife, no son
Our fool lied about Allah; we never thought anyone would
Humans sought refuge with jinn, and it only added rahaq
Like you, they thought Allah would raise no one
sections.matters: It shows the Qur’an reaching a listening heart: the jinn hear, understand, believe, and go straight back to warn their people. Their first words are tawḥīd and a clear rejection of shirk.
sections.story: The jinn were blocked from the sky and searched for the reason. A group found the Prophet ﷺ leading Fajr at Nakhlah, listened, and said: “This is what came between us and the news of the sky.” Then they returned to their people.
explained: Qul ūḥiya ilayya: the Prophet ﷺ never saw these jinn; Allah told him. A nafar, a small group, heard the recitation and called it ʿajab, amazing in eloquence and meaning. It guides to al-rushd, what is right, so they believed at once and vowed never to set up partners with their Lord.

They declared jadd rabbinā, their Lord’s majesty, far above taking a wife or son. Their foolish one, Iblīs or any fool like him, had said outrageous things about Allah. They believed it because they never imagined anyone would lie about Allah. Humans used to seek refuge with jinn, and both denied that Allah would raise anyone.
teaches: Listen to the Qur’an with full attention; it moves the heart.
Real faith comes from understanding the message, not habit or imitation.
A claim about Allah isn’t true just because leaders repeat it.
Seek refuge in Allah alone, never in jinn.
sections.hook: The surah opens with Qul, “Say”. From ayah 3 every ayah starts wa-annahu or wa-annā, “and that…”: the jinn’s statements stacked one after another, a chain that runs on to ayah 14.

sections.title: Jinn find the sky guarded; believers lose nothing, the unjust fuel Hell
sections.meaning: The jinn found the sky full of guards and flames, and could not tell what Allah intended for the earth. They admit they are divided and cannot escape Allah. Believers lose nothing; the unjust fuel Hell. Then Allah says: stay straight and receive plenty; turn away and face hard punishment.
points: The sky is full of guards; a flame waits for any eavesdropper
Is harm or guidance intended for the earth?
Some of us are righteous, some not; no one escapes Allah
We heard the guidance and believed; believers fear no loss
Muslims found the right course; the unjust are Hell’s firewood
Stay straight for abundant water; turn away for hard punishment
sections.matters: It explains what sent the jinn searching, and it breaks the belief that jinn know the unseen. It also shows that jinn, like humans, choose between faith and disbelief and face the result.
sections.story: When the Prophet ﷺ was sent, the sky was guarded so the revelation could not be stolen and passed to fortune-tellers. Ayah 16 was reportedly about Quraysh, after rain had been held back from them for seven years.
explained: Before, jinn sat in listening posts, snatching news and passing it to fortune-tellers mixed with lies. Now the sky was packed with angel guards, and a shihāb, a burning flame, lay in wait for any listener. Unsure what it meant, they said harm might be intended, or guidance from their Lord, linking only the good to Him out of respect.

They admit they are split into many paths and can’t escape Allah. They believed, and a believer fears no bakhs, lost reward, nor rahaq, unfair burden. The qāsiṭūn, who turn from the truth, feed Hell. Then Allah says: had people stayed straight, He would give them plenty as a test. Turning from His reminder brings hard punishment.
teaches: Allah guarded His revelation from the start.
Fortune-tellers’ “news” is stolen scraps mixed with lies.
Speak about Allah with good manners, linking the good to Him.
Faith costs you nothing: no good deed is lost.
Plenty is a test of gratitude, not a sign of approval.
sections.hook: Rahaq appears in ayah 6 and again in ayah 13. Page 572 ends at ayah 13; page 573 opens with ayah 14’s contrast: al-muslimūn versus al-qāsiṭūn.

sections.title: Call on none but Allah; the Prophet ﷺ only conveys His message
sections.meaning: Places of prayer belong to Allah, so call on no one beside Him. When the Prophet ﷺ stood to pray, they crowded around him. He is told to say: I call only my Lord; I can’t harm or guide you; no one can shield me from Allah; I only convey.
points: The masjids are for Allah: call on no one with Him
When Allah’s servant stood praying, they nearly crowded over him
I call only my Lord; I can’t harm or guide you
No one can protect me from Allah; no refuge but Him
My role is to convey; the disobedient face Hell forever
When they see the promise, they’ll know who is weaker
sections.matters: It puts the Messenger ﷺ in his true place: a servant who calls to Allah and conveys, with no power of his own to harm or guide. If even he cannot protect himself from Allah, no created being deserves worship.
sections.story: Reportedly the jinn asked how they could come to the masjid and pray with him while living far away, and ayah 18 came. Quraysh told him to give up his call in return for their protection, and ayah 20 answered them.
explained: Al-masājid, places of prayer, belong to Allah, so no one else is called on in them. It is also read as the whole earth, or the body parts used in sujūd. When ʿabd Allāh, the Prophet ﷺ, stood praying, they became libad, packed together: either jinn pressing close to hear, or humans and jinn uniting against him.

He states his message: I call on my Lord alone. I cannot bring you harm or guidance; that belongs to Allah. If I disobeyed Him, no one could shield me and I would find no refuge. All I have is balāgh, delivering His messages. Those who refuse will see the promise and learn whose side is weaker and smaller.
teaches: Make every duʿāʾ and act of worship for Allah alone.
Guidance is in Allah’s hands; even the Prophet ﷺ only conveyed it.
Your duty is to convey the truth, not to control the results.
Numbers and power today count for nothing on the promised Day.
sections.hook: Qul opens ayat 20, 21 and 22 back to back. Ayah 21 pairs ḍarr with rashad, just as the jinn paired sharr with rashad in ayah 10. The second ruku starts at ayah 20.

sections.title: Only Allah knows the unseen, sharing some with a chosen, guarded messenger
sections.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ does not know whether the promise is near or far off. Only Allah knows the unseen. He reveals some of it only to a messenger He chooses, and guards that revelation with angels in front and behind. He surrounds everything and has counted all things.
points: I don’t know if it is near or far off
Allah alone knows the unseen and shows it to no one
Except a chosen messenger, guarded by angels front and back
The messages arrive intact; He has counted everything
sections.matters: It closes where the surah began, with revelation and the unseen. Not jinn, not fortune-tellers, not even the Prophet ﷺ own knowledge of the unseen. A messenger receives only what Allah reveals, and it reaches him fully protected.
sections.story: Reportedly some disbelievers asked, “When will this promise come?” and ayah 25 was the reply.
explained: When they demanded a date, the Prophet ﷺ was told to say he does not know whether it is near or whether Allah has set it an amad, a long term. When a man once asked him when the Hour would be, he replied: “What have you prepared for it?”

ʿĀlim al-ghayb: Allah alone knows the unseen. He shares part of it only with a messenger He approves, as much as the mission needs, not all knowledge. He surrounds that messenger with raṣad, guard angels, so no devil can tamper with the message. He knows all that is with them and has counted every single thing.
teaches: Don’t chase dates for the Hour; prepare for it.
No one but Allah knows the unseen: not jinn, not fortune-tellers.
The revelation reached the Prophet ﷺ exactly as Allah sent it.
Allah has counted everything, down to the smallest detail.
sections.hook: Raṣadā appears in ayah 9 (the flame lying in wait) and ayah 27 (the guards). ʿAdadā ends both ayah 24 and ayah 28, the surah’s last word.

groups.text: A group of jinn heard the Qur’an, called it amazing, believed in it and vowed never to set up partners with Allah.
Allah has no wife or son. Their foolish one lied about Him, and they never thought anyone would dare.
Humans sought refuge with jinn, which only made things worse. Both thought Allah would raise no one.
The sky was now full of guards and flames. The jinn wondered whether harm or guidance was meant for the earth.
The jinn are split into different paths, and none of them can escape Allah.
They believed on hearing the guidance. Believers lose nothing; Muslims found the right course, and the unjust become Hell’s fuel.
Had people stayed straight, Allah would give them plenty, as a test. Turning from His reminder brings hard punishment.
Places of prayer are for Allah alone. When His servant stood praying, they nearly crowded over him.
The Prophet ﷺ calls only on his Lord. He cannot harm or guide anyone, and no one can shield him from Allah.
His role is to convey. Those who disobey face the Fire and will learn who is truly weak.
He does not know when the promise will come. Only Allah knows the unseen.
Allah reveals some of it to a chosen messenger, guarded by angels, and He has counted everything.

1.explain: Qul ūḥiya ilayya: the Prophet ﷺ did not see these jinn; Allah told him. A nafar, a small group, listened and told their people the Qur’an was ʿajab: amazing in eloquence and depth.
1.why: Reportedly the jinn, barred from the sky, searched for the cause. A group found the Prophet ﷺ leading Fajr at Nakhlah, on the way to ʿUkāẓ (or returning from Ṭāʾif), listened and believed. This ayah then told him what had happened.

2.explain: It guides to al-rushd, everything right in faith and in life. They believed at once and promised never to set up partners with their Lord. Their faith came from understanding it, not habit.

3.explain: Jadd rabbinā: our Lord’s majesty and greatness. One so perfect has no need of a wife or son, so they declare Him far above that.

4.explain: Safīhunā, our foolish one: Iblīs, or any fool who claimed Allah has a wife or child. Shaṭaṭ: an outrageous lie that crosses every limit.

5.explain: Their excuse for their past shirk: they never imagined humans or jinn would dare lie about Allah, so they trusted their leaders until the Qur’an showed them the truth.

6.explain: Travellers stopping in a valley used to say, “I seek refuge with the master of this valley.” It added rahaq: either the jinn grew arrogant, or they frightened humans even more.
6.why: Reportedly revealed after a shepherd, when a wolf seized a lamb, called on the valley’s jinn for protection, and an unseen voice made the wolf let it go. Another report links it to Rāfiʿ ibn ʿUmayr, who used the old refuge formula before becoming Muslim.

7.explain: The jinn thought, as you humans did, that Allah would never raise anyone: either raise the dead or send a messenger. Denying that led them into shirk.

8.explain: Lamasnā as-samāʾ: we tried to reach the sky to eavesdrop, but found it full of fierce angel guards and shuhub, burning flames.

9.explain: Before, they sat in listening posts to catch heavenly news. Now a shihāb raṣad, a flame lying in wait, destroys any listener. The sky was guarded to protect the revelation.

10.explain: They didn’t know whether this meant harm for the earth or guidance. Out of good manners they linked guidance to their Lord, and did not name who intended harm.

11.explain: Some jinn are righteous, others less so: sinners and disbelievers. Ṭarāʾiq qidadā: split into different paths and groups, just like people.

12.explain: Ẓannā here means they became certain: no one can escape Allah on earth, nor outrun Him by fleeing, even into the sky.

13.explain: Al-hudā is the Qur’an, and they were proud to believe in it. A believer fears no bakhs, losing the reward of his good deeds, and no rahaq, being wronged with extra burden.

14.explain: Some are Muslims, some qāsiṭūn: those who unjustly turn from the truth, the opposite of the just. Those who submit have aimed for the right course and found it.

15.explain: The qāsiṭūn will be ḥaṭab, firewood that feeds Hell. It is the result of their own deeds, not injustice from Allah. The jinn’s words end here.

16.explain: Now Allah speaks of people: had they kept straight on the path of Islam, He would give them māʾan ghadaqā, plentiful water, meaning abundant provision. Another view: had they kept to misguidance, He would give plenty to lead them on.
16.why: Reportedly about Quraysh, after rain had been held back from them for seven years.

17.explain: “To test them in it”: to see who stays grateful. Whoever turns from his Lord’s dhikr, the Qur’an, is driven into ʿadhāb ṣaʿad: a hard, crushing punishment with no relief.

18.explain: Al-masājid, places of prayer, belong to Allah, so call on no one with Him, in worship or in asking. It is also read as the whole earth, or the body parts that touch the ground in sujūd.
18.why: Reportedly the jinn asked the Prophet ﷺ how they could come to the masjid and pray with him while living so far away, and this ayah was revealed.

19.explain: When ʿabd Allāh, the Prophet ﷺ, stood praying, they became libad, packed together: either jinn crowding to hear, or humans and jinn uniting against him to put out his call.

20.explain: His answer: I call on my Lord alone and associate no one with Him. I reject every idol and false god besides Him.
20.why: Reportedly Quraysh told him: “You have brought something huge and made everyone your enemy. Give it up and we will protect you.” This ayah was the reply.

21.explain: I have no power to bring you harm or rashad, guidance. I am only a servant; all of that is in Allah’s hands.

22.explain: If I disobeyed Allah, no one could protect me, and I would find no multaḥad, no refuge, except with Him. If the Prophet ﷺ can’t save himself, no one else can.

23.explain: Illā balāghan: my only role, and my only safety, is delivering Allah’s messages. The everlasting Fire here is for those who disobey by refusing faith.

24.explain: They carry on until they see what they were promised, either at Badr or on the Day of Judgement. Then they will know whose helpers are weaker and fewer.

25.explain: Say: I don’t know whether the promise is near or my Lord has set it an amad, a long term. Its time is known only to Allah.
25.why: Reportedly some disbelievers asked, “When will this promise come?” and this ayah was revealed in reply.

26.explain: ʿĀlim al-ghayb: He alone knows all that is hidden, every secret and every unseen thing, and He lets no one see His unseen.

27.explain: Except a messenger He approves, whom He tells what His wisdom decides. Then He sends raṣad, guard angels, before and behind him, to keep devils away from the revelation.

28.explain: So it is known that the messengers delivered their Lord’s messages. He surrounds all that is with them and has counted every single thing by number.
